candidates.mechanism: Single-frame gap closing (c7 l.976-1002): a synthetic middle node on a gap whose end-to-start span d >= CONFIRM_MIN_SPAN must reach DeepCenter >= 0.25 or BOTH gap edges and the node are dropped (the end and the start stay open). The LAP has already paired them, so the veto only switches a chosen link on or off; nothing else competes for it. Up (9.5) lets the [8.5, 9.5) um band through without a check. Down (7.5) puts the [7.5, 8.5) band under the veto. Each flipped pair is 2 edges plus 1 node, and it merges two track fragments into one track. That is pure edge re-wiring in JT's sense, with a node change of about 0.04%. It can also save a fragment of 3-5 nodes from the length-6 filter, which adds some nodes. The metric's edge term is where a long, fast-moving track either stays joined or breaks. The veto's premise is weak for fast cells: a linear midpoint on a curved 9 um path lands off-centre and scores low on DeepCenter even when the link is right. On train the veto rejects 82% of the pairs it checks.
candidates.expected_output_change: From the exp60 lab dumps (56 train clips, 1.12M nodes, about 9.3x the public 4 clips; the exp29 public run_stats show 115 DC gap checks, about 1/9.6 of train's 1,107, so the scale holds): 5,652 accepted gap pairs, 1,107 veto checks and 904 rejections (82%). Histogram of accepted spans: [7.5,8) 293, [8,8.5) 293, [8.5,9) 66, [9,9.5) 44, [9.5,10.25] 93. Up arm: if rejections are spread evenly over spans, about 600 checks fall in [8.5,9.5) -> about +490 pairs on train -> about +50 pairs on public = +100 edges (+0.09%), +50 nodes (+0.04%), forks 0. Down arm: the 586 accepted pairs in [7.5,8.5) get checked; at the observed 82% reject rate that is up to -480 on train -> about -35 to -50 pairs on public = -70 to -100 edges, -35 to -50 nodes. Node change is far inside 1.5% in both directions.
candidates.runtime_risk: negligible. The up arm makes fewer DeepCenter lookups. The down arm adds about 60 per public clip, mostly on frames already in the 8-frame DC cache from the safe-division veto; at most tens of seconds per clip, under 0.5% of 7-8 h.

candidates.mechanism: Last gate on a safe-division proposal, after the DeepCenter veto (c7 l.1628-1632): reject when |child_dist - parent_dist| / mean > tau. Raising tau lets through forks whose two daughters sit at unequal distances from the parent. Lowering it removes the most asymmetric of today's safe forks. Each flip adds or removes one parent->daughter edge, and the division term gains or loses one fork. Nodes move only through the rule that keeps any component with a fork (a few nodes). This re-wires division edges with node counts essentially unchanged. It is also the one division knob the lab can size exactly, because it sits after the DeepCenter veto.
candidates.expected_output_change: Exact replay (tools/trainlab replay of x138's own tail) on 6 train clips with 114,271 final nodes (about the size of the public 121k): tau 0.8 -> forks +15, edges +15 (+9 or +6 or +8 per clip pair), nodes +10; tau 0.45 -> forks -16, nodes -10. Interpolating, the proposed 0.7 / 0.5 give about +8 / -9 forks on public. Against exp70g's 81 public forks that is about +/-10%, similar to one DIVINS cap step (cap4->6 was about +8 forks, +0.002). Nodes about +/-5 (0.004%).

candidates.mechanism: Strict 2-frame gap recovery (c7 l.1080-1198) links a track end at t to a track start at t+3 through 2 interpolated synthetic nodes and 3 edges. It is gated only by total span <= GAP2_MAX_TOTAL_UM (the 4.4 um step gate cannot bind below 13.2) and a direction-context check, and there is NO DeepCenter veto. The per-frame cap max(1, round(0.006*ends)) is 1 in about 99% of frames (median 6 ends per frame, >= 84 ends in 0.8% of frames). So the span limit decides which frames get a recovery and which pair wins. Up (11.7 um, 3.9 um per step) adds recoveries for faster cells in frames that today have no candidate. Down (8.7) removes the longest current recoveries; with the frame cap freed, a shorter pair in the same frame can take the slot. This moves which fragments join, edges only, with about 0.03% of nodes.

Down arm 8.7: about -200 pairs on train -> about -20 on public = -60 edges (-0.05%), -40 nodes (-0.03%). Up arm 11.7: the new (10.2, 11.7] band, if its density is similar to [8.7, 10.2], gives +100..+200 on train -> +10..+20 on public = +30..+60 edges, +20..+40 nodes. The exp29 public run had 370 gap2 candidates -> 145 selected, consistent with that. Forks 0.

candidates.mechanism: Safe-division divergence gate (c7 l.1589-1607): the candidate second daughter and the existing child must move apart by >= DIVERGE um from t+1 to t+2 (grandchild_dist - sister_dist). It is the most selective geometric gate (34,918 rejections on the 56 lab clips against 6,617 geometric candidates). Up removes safe forks whose daughters do not separate, i.e. two neighbouring cells mistaken for sisters, and cuts FP forks. Down admits slowly separating true sisters, but most of the newly admitted ones then meet the DeepCenter veto (73% reject), so the net add is damped. Each flip is one division edge, and node counts do not move.
candidates.expected_output_change: Replay on 6 clips (114k nodes): DIVERGE 3.0 -> forks -15, nodes 0 (exact, removal only). Interpolating, 2.75 gives about -8 to -10 forks on public. DIVERGE 1.5 -> +2 forks with DC-unscored candidates rejected, plus 435 candidates the kernel never DC-scored (the lab is DC-blind here, I-419). At the observed 27% DC pass rate, about 115 more reach symmetry/NN/uniqueness, so 1.75 plausibly gives +10..+30 forks on public. That is +12..+37% of forks, the riskier arm; use 2.0 instead of 1.75 if the fork change must stay under about +15. Nodes 0 in both arms.

candidates.mechanism: Same gap-1 veto as the span knob, but it changes how strict the check is instead of which pairs get checked: the synthetic midpoint of a gap spanning >= 8.5 um needs DeepCenter >= threshold. Down re-admits long gaps whose midpoint DeepCenter is lukewarm. Up kills more of the 203 long gaps that pass today. Each flip is 2 edges plus 1 node joining two fragments. This is the gap-closing counterpart of the safe-division DC threshold (closed for us), and it does not touch divisions.
candidates.expected_output_change: Not measurable offline: the lab dumps record DeepCenter scores only from the safe-division stage onward. Estimate by analogy with the safe-division DC arm (0.25 -> 0.20 flipped about 5% of rejections): down 0.15 flips about 10-20% of the 904 train rejections -> about +90..+180 train -> +10..+20 public pairs (+20..+40 edges, +10..+20 nodes). Up 0.35 drops about 20-30% of the 203 accepted -> about -5 public pairs. It is small, and the up arm may not change the output visibly; if only one arm fits, run the down arm.
candidates.runtime_risk: none (same DeepCenter lookups, only the comparison changes)

The repo default is 0.10; x138 cell 0 raised it to 0.25 as part of a holdout-selected set, and x138's PP_CANDIDATES carries 'dcgap035' (0.35, never selected because the validator is off). Every public fork uses 0.25. On the DC threshold family, the safe-division side lost in both directions on the LB (0.30 -> 0.949, 0.20 -> 0.954 vs K2 0.954), a sign that the DeepCenter scale is near-tuned at 0.25. summary: Five two-direction arms for the gap-closing / gap2 / safe-division gate group, all post-link, all node-neutral (<0.1% nodes), zero-to-negligible runtime. Output changes were sized from x138's own tail on the exp60 lab dumps (56-clip stage counters plus an exact 6-clip replay of the safe-division gates); the lab was not used for sign. Ranked: (1) DEEPCENTER_GAP_CONFIRM_MIN_SPAN_UM 8.5 -> 9.5 / 7.5, about +/-50 public gap links (+/-100 edges), the largest pure edge re-wiring in the group: the DeepCenter veto rejects 82% of the long gaps it checks. (2) SAFE_DIV_SISTER_SYMMETRY_TAU 0.6 -> 0.7 / 0.5, about +8 / -9 public forks with nodes unchanged; this is the one division knob the lab replays exactly. (3) GAP2_MAX_TOTAL_UM 10.2 -> 11.7 / 8.7, about +/-15-20 two-frame recoveries; there is no DeepCenter veto, and the per-frame cap is 1, so the span limit is the live gate. (4) SAFE_DIV_DIVERGE_UM 2.25 -> 2.75 / 1.75, about -9 / +10..30 forks; the down arm cannot be sized offline because those candidates were never DeepCenter-scored. (5) DEEPCENTER_GAP_THRESHOLD 0.25 -> 0.35 / 0.15, small, about 5-20 links. Excluded: GAP_CLOSE_UM and OUTPUT_MIN_TRACK_LEN (already LB-probed, P08 / P06+P09); rescue trigger 0.0 (+0.33% nodes, node-adding, one-directional because raising it is a no-op, lab-closed G34); SAFE_DIV_MAX_UM and SISTER_MAX (sister barely binds, -7 forks at 11; MAX's up arm cannot be sized offline); caps and EXISTING_CHILD never bind; GAP_CLOSE_REUSE_UM inert (0 reuses); GAP_REFINE shift and GAP_DENSITY_* change little; GAPFILL_* move little volume and are coupled to the readmit pool. None of the proposed knobs is in the cell-1 guard or hard-set in cell 3/4, so --set works. Notes: research/wf_ideas_v4/knobarms_28sep/arms_2.notes.md.
